ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in square $ABCD$, $AB=\sqrt{5}$. Let $E$ be a point inside square $ABCD$, with $DE=AB$ and $\angle EDC=\alpha$ $\left(0^\circ<\alpha<90^\circ\right)$. Connect $CE$ and $AE$, draw $DF\perp AE$ with the foot being point $F$, and extend $CE$ to meet $DF$ at point $G$. Connect $AG$. When $\alpha=20^\circ$, find the measure of $\angle DAE$ in degrees.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a square,\\
it follows that $\angle ADC=90^\circ$, and $AB=AD$,\\
since $\angle CDE=20^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle ADE=70^\circ$,\\
since $DE=AB$,\\
it follows that $DA=DE$,\\
therefore $\angle DAE=\angle DEA=\frac{1}{2}(180^\circ-70^\circ)=\boxed{55^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, ABCD is a square, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and D is at the upper right. Point E is located inside the square, and line segment DE connects from D obliquely downward into the interior to E, located inside the right angle enclosed by the two sides DA and DC starting from D. The figure also draws AE and CE; DF is perpendicular to AE and the foot of the perpendicular is F; the extension line of CE intersects DF at G. Reasoning: From the square, it can be known that AD = AB, and ∠ADC = 90°. The problem statement gives DE = AB, therefore DE = AD, so triangle ADE is an isosceles triangle with D as the vertex. Also because ∠EDC = α = 20°, and DE is inside ∠ADC, therefore ∠ADE = 90° - 20° = 70°. In isosceles triangle ADE, ∠DAE = ∠DEA, therefore ∠DAE = (180° - 70°) / 2 = 55°.
